lines: Records up to ten polyphonic tracks of control voltage as a standard MIDI file, one row of jacks per track
Sets the tempo written into the MIDI file, 120 BPM doubling for every volt, the same scaling Impromptu's Clocked uses; the reading is shown on the red display
Starts recording while the voltage is above 0V and stops when it falls back; with a cable here the REC button is ignored
Goes to 10V while events are actually being captured, which is after the first note when Start at first note gate is on, and as soon as recording starts when it is off
The note pitch for that track, 1V per octave, one note per polyphonic channel; 0V is middle C and the pitch is rounded to the nearest semitone
The note gates for that track, one per polyphonic channel, a note sounding while the channel is at 1V or above
The note velocities for that track, one per polyphonic channel, 0-10V by default and rescaled by the VEL Input Range menu; unpatched, every note is recorded at velocity 100
The aftertouch for that track, 0-10V by default and rescaled by the AFT Input Range menu; only the first channel is read, and that one value is written to every note of the track
The pitchbend for that track, -5V to 5V by default and rescaled by the PW Input Range menu; one channel only, and it is always written as a 14-bit value
The modulation wheel for that track, 0-10V by default and rescaled by the MW Input Range menu; one channel only, sent as control change 1, or as 1 and 33 with MW is 14bit turned on
Note — nothing is written until a target file is chosen; pick one from Output File on the menu, or a file dialog opens the first time you record
Note — the REC button starts and stops the recording and turns red while it is running; it is not a parameter, so no click on it reaches this help
Note — a cable in the REC jack takes the button out of use altogether
Note — a track is recorded only when at least one jack in its row has a cable in it
Note — with a cable in a row's gate jack and none in its pitch jack, each polyphonic channel gets a note of its own, from middle C upwards by a semitone, which suits drum gates
Note — the MIDI file is written when recording stops, so stop the recorder before looking for the file
Note — the lamp under the ACTIVE jack is lit whenever that output is high
Note — a MIDIRecorderCC placed immediately to the right adds control change columns to the same ten tracks, and several can be chained one after another
Menu — Output File — chooses the MIDI file to write; the path is shown in place of Select... once one has been chosen
Menu — Append -001, -002, etc. — writes a new numbered file each time rather than overwriting the one already there
Menu — Start at first note gate — holds the recording back until the first note gate arrives, so events line up with a bar; earlier pitchbend, modulation and aftertouch are dropped
Menu — VEL Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the velocity jacks, from -10 to 10 down to 0 to 1
Menu — AFT Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the aftertouch jacks
Menu — PW Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the pitchbend jacks
Menu — MW Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the modulation jacks
Menu — MW is 14bit — writes the modulation value as control change 1 and 33 together, at 14-bit resolution, instead of control change 1 alone

MIDIRecorder.notes: CVRange::to7bit and to14bit divide by high rather than by high minus low (CVRange.hpp:14 and 19), so every bipolar range option is wrong: with the -5 to 5 range, which is the pitchbend default, 0V already reads as the maximum and only -5V to 0V has any effect. The unipolar ranges, including all four defaults except pitchbend, are correct. The README calls AFT polyphonic, but the code reads it with getVoltage (MIDIRecorder.cpp:440 and 458), so only channel 0 is used and its value is written to every channel of the track. The Start/Stop parameter (index 0) has no widget: the REC button is a custom SvgButton that sets its own flag, and the parameter is never read (the line that would read it is commented out at MIDIRecorder.cpp:576). The Text Style parameter (index 1) has no widget either; it is set from the Text Color menu that every module in this plugin carries.

lines: An expander for the MIDI Recorder: five more columns of control voltage, each recorded as a MIDI control change on the recorder's ten tracks
Sends the voltage here as a control change on the track of its row, under the control number shown at the top of its column, 0-10V mapped to 0 to 127 unless that column's Input Range says otherwise
Note — this module records nothing on its own: it has to stand immediately to the right of a MIDI Recorder, or to the right of another MIDIRecorderCC that leads back to one
Note — any number of these can be chained one after another to the right of the recorder
Note — the five red displays at the top show the control number each column is recorded under; the columns start at control change 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, and each is changed from that column's menu
Note — a row is recorded only when at least one jack in it has a cable, and only while the recorder itself is running
Note — values are sampled 200 times a second, the rate the MIDI baud rate allows
Note — nothing stops two columns from writing the same control number; with a column set to 14 bits at control change 2 and another set to control change 34, both write to control change 34
Menu — CC#1 — opens the settings for the first column: its Input Range, its 14bit switch and its MIDI CC number
Menu — CC#2 — opens the settings for the second column
Menu — CC#3 — opens the settings for the third column
Menu — CC#4 — opens the settings for the fourth column
Menu — CC#5 — opens the settings for the fifth column
Menu — Input Range — in a column's submenu: sets the voltage span read from that column's jacks, from -10 to 10 down to 0 to 1
Menu — 14bit — in a column's submenu: writes that column at 14-bit resolution as two control changes, the chosen number and that number plus 32; the second one is dropped if it would go past 127
Menu — MIDI CC — in a column's submenu: a box for typing that column's control change number

lines: Turns twelve drum gates into one polyphonic track of General MIDI drum notes, gates and velocities
A gate for the drum named above it; while a cable is in this jack that drum takes a channel on all three outputs, and the voltage here is passed straight to the gate output
Sets the velocity of the drum named above it, passed straight through as a voltage on the velocity output; unpatched, that channel carries the voltage for velocity 100
The note of each triggered drum, 1V per octave, one channel per gate jack that has a cable in it
The gate of each triggered drum, passed through from its gate jack, one channel per gate jack that has a cable in it
The velocity of each triggered drum, one channel per gate jack that has a cable in it
Note — click the name above a pair of jacks to choose which General MIDI drum that pair sends; the names are drawn by the module, not parameters, so no click on them reaches this help
Note — channels are packed: only jacks with a cable get a channel on the outputs, and they are numbered in panel order from the top left
Note — the module starts on kick, low tom, snare, mid tom, side stick, high tom, pedal hi-hat, hand clap, closed hi-hat, crash, open hi-hat and ride
Note — the three outputs are made to be patched into a MIDI Recorder row or into Rack's own CV-MIDI

Harp.notes: Two things in the source do not match the README. The default scale, used when the scale jack is unpatched, repeats after eleven semitones rather than twelve (Harp.cpp:103 sets scaleSize to 11 with the comment "default to chromatic"), so the unpatched module is not chromatic. And the note-range parameter is configured with a minimum of 2, a maximum of 16 and a default of 48 (Harp.cpp:60), which looks like the arguments transposed; the menu offers 2 to 48 and writes the parameter directly rather than through its quantity, so the larger values do work, but a new module starts at 48.
